title: Adaptive Caching for Structured Search
question: What effect did adaptive caching have on latency and answer quality?
paper:
### PAPER: Adaptive Caching for Structured Search
<abstract>
We study a cache for repeated structured queries.
</abstract>
The benchmark used 2,000 fixed questions and three random seeds. Adaptive caching reduced median retrieval latency from 420 milliseconds to 260 milliseconds. Exact-answer accuracy remained 81.4 percent with and without caching. The ablation disabled cache reuse between unrelated queries.
reference_evidence: Adaptive caching reduced median retrieval latency from 420 milliseconds to 260 milliseconds. Exact-answer accuracy remained 81.4 percent with and without caching.

title: Branch Allocation Under Sparse Rewards
question: Which allocation policy improved success, and what tradeoff did it incur?
paper:
### PAPER: Branch Allocation Under Sparse Rewards
<abstract>
We compare uniform and uncertainty-directed branch allocation.
</abstract>
Uniform allocation evaluated four continuations at every state. Uncertainty-directed allocation improved held-out success from 37 percent to 46 percent. It increased the ninety-fifth percentile rollout time by 12 percent because difficult states received more continuations. Total training tokens were held constant.
reference_evidence: Uncertainty-directed allocation improved held-out success from 37 percent to 46 percent. It increased the ninety-fifth percentile rollout time by 12 percent because difficult states received more continuations.

title: Replay Equivalence in Typed Workflows
question: How often did sliced replay disagree with full replay?
paper:
### PAPER: Replay Equivalence in Typed Workflows
<abstract>
Typed dataflow dependencies support partial workflow replay.
</abstract>
We evaluated 10,000 interventions over deterministic workflow fixtures. Sliced replay and full-suffix replay produced byte-identical terminal artifacts for all 10,000 interventions. The observed disagreement count was zero. Floating-point artifacts were serialized canonically before comparison.
reference_evidence: Sliced replay and full-suffix replay produced byte-identical terminal artifacts for all 10,000 interventions. The observed disagreement count was zero.
